title: Action de Galois sur Teichmüller : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (from pp. 47-49). Σ is the Riemann sphere P^1(C), J = {0,1,∞} is the set of three marked points R_i, and Σ* = Σ \ J. Σ̃ is the real oriented blow-up of Σ at the R_i: a compact surface with three boundary circles U_i (the transcription's V_i). Each U_i is the circle of tangent directions at R_i, i.e. the unit circle in T_{Σ,R_i}. The interior Σ̃^0 = Σ̃ \ ∂Σ̃ is identified with Σ*.

On the previous page, inclusion into Σ̃ gives equivalences of covering categories Rev(Σ̃) ≃ Rev(Σ*), hence (14) Π_1(Σ̃) → Π_1(Σ*) on fundamental groupoids 'au sens large'. Composing with Π_1(U_i) → Π_1(Σ̃) gives (15) Π_1(U_i) → Π_1(Σ*).

This page makes two points.

(1) Which base 'points' (objects of the groupoid) will be used. The fibre functor on coverings is evaluated either at genuine points of Σ̃ or at subsets of Σ̃ that are connected and simply connected for the induced topology. Genuine points are either points of Σ* or points of a boundary circle U_i; the latter are tangential base points in their topological incarnation. Simply connected subsets include simply connected regions of Σ* (for example the two open hemispheres cut out by the real circle Σ_R). These are made to 'overflow' (déborder) naturally onto the boundary of Σ̃, by adjoining the boundary arcs of directions pointing into the region. A covering restricted to such a subset is trivial, so its set of sections gives a well-defined fibre functor and therefore an object of the fundamental groupoid with many base points.

(2) Symmetry. A group Γ acts on the pair (Σ, J). From the next page, which introduces Σ_R, the hemispheres ε ∈ π_0(Σ \ Σ_R) and the orientations ω, Γ is presumably the group of holomorphic and antiholomorphic automorphisms of P^1 preserving {0,1,∞}, i.e. S_3 × Z/2 (complex conjugation). By transport of structure Γ acts on Σ̃ → Σ, J ⊂ Σ, and hence on (14) and (15). Grothendieck stresses as 'an essential aspect of the work' that notation and constructions (choices of base points, paths, generators) be invariant under these operations.

The next page carries this out with a Γ-stable configuration:
- the antipodes Q_i of the R_i;
- the poles P_ε of the two hemispheres;
- the tangential points R_i^ω (real directions) and S_i^ε (directions into each hemisphere) on the circles U_i;
- canonical bijections of these with ω and ε.

Purpose: to obtain an explicit, symmetry-adapted description of the (profinite completion of the) fundamental groupoid of P^1 − {0,1,∞} with several base points, so that the action of Gal(Q̄/Q), commuting with this symmetry, can be written in coordinates. This is the germ of what became Ihara's and Drinfeld's GT-type description.
errors: 'éléments de Π_1(Σ̃)' should really be 'objets' of the groupoid (base points / fibre functors), not elements; a terminological slip.

For a subset to define a fibre functor it must be connected (path-connected) as well as simply connected for the induced topology; 'parties 1-connexes' implicitly includes this, so this is not a real error.
Neither this page nor the next states the group Γ explicitly; that it is S_3 × Z/2 (including complex conjugation) is an inference from the next page.

ideas.what: Fundamental groupoid of Σ̃ (oriented real blow-up) with base 'points' including boundary points of the blown-up circles
ideas.modern_name: Tangential base points (topological version via real oriented blow-up)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Deligne 1989 (Le groupe fondamental de la droite projective moins trois points); also Ihara, Anderson
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme discusses base points for the Teichmüller tower in general terms; no explicit oriented-blow-up construction there that I know of

ideas.what: Using simply connected subsets (e.g. hemispheres) as base 'points', extended ('débordées') to the boundary of Σ̃
ideas.modern_name: Fundamental groupoid based at simply connected regions / contractible base sets
ideas.usually_credited_to: Deligne 1989 (simply connected domains as base points); Brown (groupoids on sets of base points)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (choice of base points in Teichmüller groupoids), in spirit only

ideas.what: Requirement that the base-point system and notation be invariant under the symmetry group of (P^1, {0,1,∞}), including complex conjugation
ideas.modern_name: S_3 × Z/2-equivariant fundamental groupoid; symmetric base points (the source of the 2-cycle/3-cycle relations in GT)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Drinfeld 1990, Ihara (GT relations); Esquisse d'un programme for the general programme
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (1984), emphasis on symmetric base points and on the 'opérations' of the symmetry groups on the Teichmüller tower

missed.claim: An early (≥1978, pre-Esquisse, pre-Deligne 1989) systematic set-up of the fundamental groupoid of P^1−{0,1,∞} on a mixed base: interior points, tangential points on blown-up boundary circles, and simply connected regions extended to the boundary. The whole base is chosen equivariantly under S_3 × complex conjugation. This anticipates Deligne's tangential/simply-connected base points and the symmetric set-up behind GT, but it is a documentation and priority point rather than a new result.
missed.quote: soit de parties de Σ̃ qui sont 1-connexes pour la top. induite par Σ̃ ... et en les faisant "déborder" sur Σ̃ de façon naturelle
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Mainly historical: it documents Grothendieck's independent use of tangential and region-based base points, with real-structure (complex conjugation) equivariance built in from the start. The latter is somewhat less emphasised in the Drinfeld/Ihara literature.

deep.surprise_reason: The ideas (tangential base points via oriented blow-up, simply connected regions as base points, S_3 × Z/2-equivariant choices) are now standard through Deligne, Ihara and Drinfeld. The page is of interest mainly for priority and dating: it shows Grothendieck setting this up carefully, with explicit attention to complex conjugation, before those works. It contains no new theorem.
